Briefed with the ticket, re-resolved governing ADRs (note: the ticket's `ADR-021-out-of-band-service-migrations.md` link is stale — the real file is ADR-022), and key code pointers.

# TKT-71 Execution Plan — Bound the completion-outbox backfill

## 1. Chosen approach

**Option 3: move the backfill behind the drainer. No index, no marker, no batching.**

`run()` stops calling `BackfillCompletionOutbox` under the 30s `mctx`. Instead, the outbox
drainer gains a **one-shot, deferred backfill pass**: it fires once, after the first successful
`DrainOnce`, and only if the service has been up long enough that any live checkout completing
before the outbox existed would already have been published (in practice: on the first drain
tick, ~5s after boot). The store function is retitled `BackfillCompletionOutboxOnce` to make
the "not every boot" property legible at the call site; its body is unchanged.

Why the other three lose:

- **Option 1 (index on `orders(status, guest_order_ref)` for the boot scan)** — solves only the
  scan, not the unbounded `todo` slice or the 30s deadline. It also writes a permanent index to
  keep a once-ever query cheap: after the first drain, the predicate matches zero rows and the
  index is write amplification forever. ADR-020's "plain `CREATE INDEX`" rule applies, but the
  real objection is that the index pays rent on a problem that disappears after one run.
- **Option 2 (`completion_outbox_backfilled` marker)** — turns an idempotent scan into a
  stateful "did we run yet" flag. That is a second source of truth about whether owed events
  exist, and it can lie: a crash between owing an event and stamping the marker leaves a paid
  order silently unprotected. The ticket's own COS names the guarantee this backfill protects;
  a marker makes the guarantee contingent on a row the drainer never looks at.
- **Option 4 (bounded/batched pass under the deadline)** — keeps the fail-fast startup coupling.
  "Bounded to 30s" still means a slow backfill is commerce downtime, which is the pathology
  TKT-66 existed to remove. It also leaves the service listening later than it needs to.

Moving it into the migrate job is out: ADR-022 §Consequences already says why (a restarted
container re-runs `run()` but not the job, so the job placement would pay the scan once per
deploy but still leave the 30s fail-fast coupling on boot).

**Reversibility:** high. Deleting the deferred call and restoring the `mctx` call is a
~10-line revert in `main.go`; no schema, no marker row, no data migration to unwind.

## 2. DoD

- [ ] Commerce's `run()` no longer calls `BackfillCompletionOutbox` before `srv.ListenAndServe`.
- [ ] The drainer runs the backfill exactly once, after its first drain pass, outside any
  request or startup deadline.
- [ ] `TestBackfillOwesEventsForPreExistingCompletedOrders` still passes (the COS test).
- [ ] A new smoke test proves the COS: a process that starts against an unmigrated commerce DB
  (no `completion_outbox` table) becomes healthy **without** failing on the backfill, and the
  backfill is observable in the drainer's logs once the table exists.
- [ ] `make check` (including the commerce outbox smoke suite) is green.

## 3. Files to touch

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `services/commerce/internal/store/store.go` | Rename `BackfillCompletionOutbox` → `BackfillCompletionOutboxOnce`; update the doc comment to say it is invoked once by the drainer, not at startup; keep the body byte-identical. No signature change. |
| `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go` | Delete the `mctx` + `BackfillCompletionOutbox` call (lines ~130–140) and the "keeps its own bound" comment. Wire the one-shot into the drainer's `Run` (see below). |
| `services/commerce/internal/outbox/drainer.go` | Add a `sync.Once`-guarded `runBackfill` field and a `backfill func(context.Context) error` constructor param. `Run` calls `DrainOnce`, then `go d.runBackfill(ctx)` once, then enters the ticker loop. `runBackfill` calls the store function with a background-derived context (no deadline) and logs `ErrorContext` on failure — it never returns the error to `Run`. |
| `services/commerce/internal/store/outbox_smoke_test.go` | Add `TestBackfillRunsOnceBehindDrainer` (see §4). Existing `TestBackfillOwesEventsForPreExistingCompletedOrders` updates its call site to the new name; assertions unchanged. |
| `smoke/smoke_test.go` | Add `TestCommerceStartsWithoutRunningBackfill` (see §4). |

Nothing under `services/commerce/internal/store/migrations/` changes — no new schema, no index,
no marker table. ADR-008/ADR-022 stay untouched.

## 4. Test seam & test plan

**Seam:** `outboxDB` (real Postgres via `COMMERCE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`) and the drainer's
existing `store.OutboxDB` interface. The drainer test in
`services/commerce/internal/outbox/drainer_test.go` already uses a fake `OutboxDB`; the new
once-behavior is asserted there without a database.

**TDD:** all three tests below are writable against the current code and go red on it:

1. `TestBackfillRunsOnceBehindDrainer` (`outbox/drainer_test.go`) — fake `OutboxDB` whose
   `QueryContext` returns two owed rows. Construct the drainer with a `backfill` stub that
   counts invocations. Call `Run` with a cancellable context, cancel after one tick, assert
   the stub ran exactly once and only after `ClaimOutbox` was called. **Red today:** the
   constructor has no `backfill` param and `Run` never invokes one.
2. `TestBackfillOwesEventsForPreExistingCompletedOrders` (`store/outbox_smoke_test.go`) —
   unchanged behavior, renamed call. Still passes; it is the COS regression net.
3. `TestCommerceStartsWithoutRunningBackfill` (`smoke/smoke_test.go`) — point the commerce
   binary at an empty database, start it, assert `/healthz` returns 200 within the 30s window
   and that stderr does **not** contain `backfill completion outbox`. **Red today:** the
   startup path attempts the backfill and fails the process when the table is missing.

The third test is the one that proves the COS "startup does no unbounded data work / the bound
is explicit and cannot fail the service": the service listens and serves health while the
backfill has not run, so the backfill can no longer be a startup failure mode.

## 5. Risks & pre-mortem

**How this could break paid-but-no-ticket:**

- **The deferred backfill silently doesn't run.** If the drainer constructor is mis-wired or
  the `sync.Once` is dropped in a refactor, orders completed before the outbox existed stay
  un-owed forever. Guard: `TestBackfillRunsOnceBehindDrainer` asserts the call happens; the
  smoke suite's `TestBackfillOwesEventsForPreExistingCompletedOrders` still proves the store
  function works when called.
- **The backfill runs before the schema exists.** If commerce is started against an unmigrated
  database, the deferred pass errors and is logged. Guard: it is logged as an error, not
  swallowed; the next boot retries because `sync.Once` is per-process. The service stays up,
  which is strictly better than today's fail-fast.
- **A checkout completing during the backfill window.** The predicate is
  `x.order_id IS NULL`, so a live `CompleteOrder` that inserts its own outbox row is not
  matched; the backfill only ever sees rows no live path will touch. Guard: the existing
  idempotency assertion in the smoke test covers the same `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` path.
- **The 5s drain interval delays ticket issuance for historical orders.** Acceptable: those
  orders have been paid-but-no-ticket since before the outbox existed; a 5s delay on first boot
  is noise against that baseline.

## 6. Open decisions

1. **Should the drainer retry the backfill if the first pass errors?** The plan logs and moves
   on; a retry loop would need a backoff policy and is arguably TKT-71 scope creep. Reviewer
   should rule whether "log once, stay up" is sufficient or whether a bounded retry belongs in
   this change.
2. **Is the `sync.Once` per-process enough, or should the "once" be durable?** A durable marker
   (Option 2) was rejected above, but a reviewer who disagrees should say so now rather than
   after implementation.

description:
**Found by the Codex adversarial review on TKT-66 (PR #50)**, which called it
"a startup-critical data migration with worse scaling characteristics than the ADR admits". It was
right, and [ADR-021](docs/adr/ADR-021-out-of-band-service-migrations.md) now names it as the known
exception rather than claiming the startup path is clean.

[ADR-021](docs/adr/ADR-021-out-of-band-service-migrations.md) moved migrations off the server path
into one-shot jobs. `BackfillCompletionOutbox`
(`services/commerce/internal/store/store.go:193`, called `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go`)
deliberately stayed — it is data repair, not schema, it is idempotent, and the migrate job has
already applied the schema it reads. That call was taken at the TKT-66 plan gate and is not
re-litigated here.

**But it retains exactly the pathology TKT-66 existed to remove**, for commerce only:

- it **scans on every boot** — `orders o JOIN reservations r LEFT JOIN completion_outbox x
  WHERE o.status='completed' AND o.guest_order_ref IS NOT NULL AND x.order_id IS NULL`. Once drained
  it *matches* nothing, but it still scans;
- it **buffers every match in memory** (the `todo` slice) — unbounded in the number of orders owed;
- it runs under `main.go`'s **30-second deadline**, and any error **fails the service before it
  listens**. A slow backfill is therefore commerce downtime, which is the sentence ADR-008's
  Consequences and ADR-021's Context both call the problem.

Bounded today: the predicate is narrow and the table is small. It is a real ceiling on a populated
orders table — the same "correct today, fatal later" shape ADR-020 recorded for index builds.

**Not urgent** — no deployment exists and no table is populated (the same reasons TKT-66 bought only
a future option). File it so the ceiling is written down rather than re-derived a third time.

**Options to weigh:** an index backing the predicate so the boot-time scan is cheap; a
`completion_outbox_backfilled` marker so it runs once instead of scanning every boot; moving it
behind the drainer (it already polls the same table) so startup does no data work at all; or a
bounded/batched pass that cannot exceed the deadline. Note moving it into the migrate job does
**not** help — the service waits on that job anyway.

**COS:** commerce startup does no unbounded data work, or the bound is explicit and cannot fail the
service; the paid-but-no-ticket guarantee the backfill protects is preserved, with
`TestBackfillOwesEventsForPreExistingCompletedOrders`
(`services/commerce/internal/store/outbox_smoke_test.go:344`) still green.
